_note: Update 57: grammar extras — 80 questions on all 12 tenses by name, 50 on active and passive voice in every tense (MAP Language Usage style).

questions.stem: Choose the verb that best completes the sentence in the past simple: Yesterday, Omar ____ his bike to school.
options: is riding
will ride
rides
rode
questions.why: The past simple (rode) tells about a finished action, and "yesterday" signals the past.

questions.stem: Sort each sentence about Huda's reading habits by its tense.

rows.text: Huda reads a book every night.
Huda finished a book about camels last night.
Huda will read a new book tomorrow.

questions.why: "Every night" signals the present simple, "last night" the past simple, and "will" + verb the future simple.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses the future simple correctly?
options: Next week, Sara has visited her grandmother in Abha.
Next week, Sara will visit her grandmother in Abha.
Next week, Sara was visiting her grandmother in Abha.
Next week, Sara visited her grandmother in Abha.
questions.why: The future simple is will + base verb (will visit), which matches "next week."

questions.stem: Find and fix the verb error in this sentence about Faisal's football game.
questions.why: "Last Friday" tells us the action is finished, so the past simple "kicked" is needed.

questions.stem: True or false: In the sentence "The children are playing in the sand right now," the verb is in the present progressive.
questions.why: Am/is/are + an -ing verb (are playing) is the present progressive, used for actions happening now.

questions.stem: Which sentences about Ali's art class are in the present progressive? Choose two.
options: Ali drew a camel for art class.
The students watch a video about colors on Mondays.
The students are watching a video about colors.
Ali is drawing a camel for art class.
questions.why: The present progressive uses is/are + an -ing verb.

questions.stem: Match each sentence about the family trip to AlUla to its tense.

pairs.left: We were driving through the desert at sunrise.
We will be staying at a camp tonight.
We are taking photos of the rocks.

questions.why: Progressive tenses use a form of be + -ing: was/were (past), am/is/are (present), will be (future).

questions.stem: Choose the verb that correctly completes the past progressive sentence: Reem ____ her homework when the lights went out.
options: was doing
is doing
will do
has done
questions.why: The past progressive (was doing) shows an action in progress when another past action happened.

questions.stem: Put these sentences about Noor's bean plants in order from past to present to future.
sequence: Last week, Noor planted bean seeds.
Today, Noor is measuring the small plants.
Next week, Noor will share her results with the class.
questions.why: Planted (past simple) comes first, is measuring (present progressive) is now, and will share (future simple) is later.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses the present progressive correctly?
options: The falcon flying above the dunes is now.
The falcon is fly above the dunes now.
The falcon is flying above the dunes now.
The falcon are flying above the dunes now.
questions.why: A singular subject takes is + the -ing verb: is flying.

questions.stem: Choose the verb that best completes the sentence in the present perfect: Khalid ____ three books about space this month.
options: have read
was read
reading
has read
questions.why: The present perfect is has/have + past participle; a singular subject takes has.

questions.stem: Select the sentence about the Red Sea field trip that uses the past perfect.

segments.text: The class visited the aquarium in Jeddah.
Before the bus arrived, the students had packed their lunches.
The guide is showing them a sea turtle.
They will write reports tomorrow.

questions.why: Had + past participle (had packed) is the past perfect.

questions.stem: Classify each sentence about Lina's swimming lessons as present perfect or past simple.

rows.text: Lina has learned to swim on her back.
Lina learned to dive last summer.
Lina has never missed a lesson.
Lina missed one lesson in May.

questions.why: Has + past participle is the present perfect; a past form with a finished time (last summer, in May) is the past simple.

questions.stem: Read the sentence: "By the time the match started, the fans had filled the stadium." Which tense is the verb "had filled"?

partA.stem: Read the sentence: "By the time the match started, the fans had filled the stadium." Which tense is the verb "had filled"?

partB.stem: Which phrase in the sentence about the fans signals that tense?

options.label: B
options.text: By the time the match started

questions.why: "By the time" + a past event signals the past perfect for the action that was finished earlier.

questions.stem: Choose the verb that correctly completes the past simple sentence: Last night, Hassan ____ his brother's bicycle.
options: is fixing
will fix
fixed
fixes
questions.why: "Last night" is a finished time, so the past simple "fixed" is correct.

questions.stem: Fix the tense error in this sentence about Yousef's model volcano.
questions.why: The present perfect cannot be used with a finished time like "two days ago"; use the past simple.

questions.stem: Which sentences about the school garden are in the present perfect? Choose two.
options: The students planted ten palm seedlings yesterday.
The students have planted ten palm seedlings.
Mr. Saleh is watering the herbs right now.
Mr. Saleh has already watered the herbs.
questions.why: Has/have + past participle forms the present perfect.

questions.stem: Choose the verb that best completes the sentence: Ahmed ____ in Riyadh since 2019.
options: lives
lived
has lived
is living
questions.why: "Since" + a starting point signals the present perfect (has lived).

questions.stem: True or false: The sentence "Maha will bake date cookies for the class party" is in the future simple.
questions.why: Will + base verb (will bake) is the future simple.

questions.stem: Match each time expression from Faris's weekly planner to the tense it most often signals.
questions.why: Time words are clues: since → present perfect, yesterday → past, tomorrow → future, right now → present progressive, every → present simple.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses the future progressive correctly?
options: At eight tonight, Dana was be watching the eclipse.
At eight tonight, Dana will be watching the eclipse.
At eight tonight, Dana will be watch the eclipse.
At eight tonight, Dana will watching the eclipse.
questions.why: The future progressive is will be + an -ing verb.

questions.stem: Classify each sentence about the robotics club by its tense.

rows.text: The team is testing its robot today.
The team was testing its robot when the bell rang.
The team will be testing its robot all afternoon tomorrow.
Two members were writing code while the others watched.

questions.why: Is/are + -ing is present progressive, was/were + -ing is past progressive, and will be + -ing is future progressive.

questions.stem: Correct the verb error in this sentence about Nasser's football practice.
questions.why: The sentence is set in the past, so the interrupting action must be past simple: blew.

questions.stem: Which sentences correctly use the past perfect to show the earlier of two past events? Choose two.
options: Salma has studied the map before the hike began.
When we reached the oasis, the camels have already drunk.
When we reached the oasis, the camels had already drunk.
Salma had studied the map before the hike began.
questions.why: Use had + past participle for the earlier of two past actions, not has/have.

questions.stem: Read: "Before Mariam presented her project, she had practiced her speech twice. After she had presented, the judges asked questions. Later, she received a medal." Put Mariam's science fair events in the order they happened.
questions.why: The past perfect (had practiced) marks the action that happened first.

questions.stem: Choose the verb that best completes the present progressive sentence: Look! The dolphins ____ next to our boat.
options: are swimming
swim
swam
have swum
questions.why: "Look!" shows the action is happening now, so use the present progressive.

questions.stem: True or false: In "Abdullah had finished his chores before his cousins arrived," the verb "had finished" is in the present perfect.
questions.why: Had + past participle is the past perfect; the present perfect uses has/have.

questions.stem: Choose the verb that best completes the sentence: By next June, Lina ____ in Dammam for ten years.
options: has been living
had lived
will live
will have lived
questions.why: "By next June" + a length of time points to the future perfect: will have lived.

questions.stem: Select the two sentences about Grandfather's pearl-diving days that use the past progressive. Select two sentences.

segments.text: One morning, Grandfather was diving near the reef when a storm began.
He often tells us about the old boats.
The divers were singing as they pulled the ropes.
Now he has a small shop in Dammam.

questions.why: Was/were + an -ing verb (was diving, were singing) is the past progressive.

questions.stem: Match each sentence about Turki's desert hike to its tense.

pairs.left: Turki has hiked this trail twice.
Turki had hiked for an hour before he rested.
Turki will have hiked ten kilometers by noon.

questions.why: Has + participle = present perfect, had + participle = past perfect, will have + participle = future perfect.

questions.stem: Classify each sentence about the school basketball final by its verb form.

rows.text: The players trained hard all week.
The fans are cheering loudly.
The team has won five games in a row.
The center had blocked every shot.
The coach was shouting instructions.

questions.why: Progressive forms use be + -ing; perfect forms use have/has/had + past participle.

questions.stem: Choose the verb that best completes the sentence: Rakan ____ chess for two hours when his father called him for dinner.
options: has been playing
is playing
had been playing
will have been playing
questions.why: The past perfect progressive shows an action that continued up to another past event.

questions.stem: Correct the error in this sentence about Jana's research on Al-Biruni.
questions.why: Use "for" with a length of time and "since" with a starting point.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses the present perfect progressive correctly?
options: The scientists are been studying the coral reef since March.
The scientists have being studying the coral reef since March.
The scientists has been studying the coral reef since March.
The scientists have been studying the coral reef since March.
questions.why: The present perfect progressive is have/has been + -ing, and a plural subject takes have.

questions.stem: Which sentences about Dalia's weather journal use the present perfect progressive? Choose two.
options: Dalia has been recording the temperature every hour.
Her classmates have been helping her collect data.
Dalia had been recording the temperature before lunch.
Her classmates will have been helping her for a week.
questions.why: Has/have been + -ing is the present perfect progressive; had been is past and will have been is future.

questions.stem: True or false: In "By the end of the day, the volunteers will have planted 200 mangrove trees," the verb is in the future perfect.
questions.why: Will have + past participle is the future perfect.

questions.stem: Match each sentence about Hamad's falcon to its tense.

pairs.left: The falcon has been training since dawn.
The falcon had been resting before the flight.
By noon, the falcon will have been flying for an hour.

questions.why: Has/have been, had been, and will have been + -ing form the three perfect progressive tenses.

questions.stem: Read: "By the time Bader arrived at the lab at ten, his partner had been preparing slides for two hours. Before she started the slides, she had cleaned the microscope. Bader then looked at the cells and drew them." Put the events in the lab in the order they happened.
sequence: Bader looked at the cells and drew them.
questions.why: Past perfect verbs (had cleaned, had been preparing) describe actions completed or begun before Bader arrived.

questions.stem: Choose the verb that best completes the sentence: Next Saturday at noon, while their families wait below, the hikers ____ up Jabal Sawda.
options: were climbing
will be climbing
have climbed
had climbed
questions.why: The future progressive (will be climbing) shows an action in progress at a future moment.

questions.stem: Select the sentence about the Riyadh book fair that uses the future perfect progressive.

segments.text: Many visitors have come to the book fair this week.
By Friday, Huda will have been volunteering there for six days.
She was helping at the poetry booth yesterday.
She will be meeting an author tomorrow.

questions.why: Will have been + -ing is the future perfect progressive.

questions.stem: Read the sentence: "Omar was tired because he had been studying for the chemistry test all night." What tense is "had been studying"?

partA.stem: Read the sentence: "Omar was tired because he had been studying for the chemistry test all night." What tense is "had been studying"?

partB.stem: Which statement best explains why that tense fits Omar's sentence?

options.label: A
options.text: It shows an action that is still going on right now.

options.label: B
options.text: It shows a single action completed in one moment.

options.label: C
options.text: It shows an action that will finish in the future.

options.label: D
options.text: It shows an action that continued up to a past moment.

questions.why: The past perfect progressive shows an ongoing action that lasted until another point in the past.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses the past progressive correctly?
options: The girls were painting a mural when the principal walked in.
The girls were paint a mural when the principal walked in.
The girls were painting a mural when the principal was walk in.
The girls was painting a mural when the principal walked in.
questions.why: The past progressive is was/were + -ing; a plural subject takes were.

questions.stem: Correct the tense error in this sentence about the tourists at Hegra.
questions.why: An action finished before another past action needs the past perfect: had bought.

questions.stem: Classify each sentence about Laila's year in Canada by its tense.

rows.text: Laila had learned some French before she moved.
She had been living in Toronto for a month when it first snowed.
By December, she will have been studying there for a year.
Her brother had never seen snow before that winter.

questions.why: Had + participle is past perfect; had been + -ing is past perfect progressive; will have been + -ing is future perfect progressive.

questions.stem: Which sentences about the student robotics team correctly use the future perfect? Choose two.
options: The engineers will had tested the motor before the competition.
By Thursday, the team will have build the robot's arm.
By Thursday, the team will have built the robot's arm.
The engineers will have tested the motor before the competition.
questions.why: The future perfect is will have + past participle (built, tested).

questions.stem: Choose the verb that best completes the present simple sentence: Abeer ____ her grandmother every Friday.
options: visiting
visit
visits
is visit
questions.why: With a singular subject and a habit (every Friday), the present simple adds -s: visits.

questions.stem: Match each sentence about the Jeddah Corniche cleanup to its tense.

pairs.left: Volunteers collect trash there every month.
Volunteers will collect more bags next week.
Volunteers have collected trash there since 2018.

questions.why: Time clues (every month, last year, next week, since) help identify each tense.

questions.stem: True or false: The sentence "Majid has been waiting for the bus for twenty minutes" is in the present perfect progressive.
questions.why: Has been + -ing is the present perfect progressive, used for an action that started in the past and continues now.

questions.stem: Order these sentences about the date palm farmer from the earliest action to the latest action.
sequence: The farmer had planted the palms years before the drought.
During the drought, he was carrying water to them every day.
Now the palms are producing sweet dates.
Next autumn, he will be selling the dates at the market.
questions.why: Past perfect comes before past progressive, then present progressive, then future progressive.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses the past perfect progressive correctly?
options: The divers had been explore the reef for an hour when they saw a shark.
The divers have been exploring the reef for an hour when they saw a shark.
The divers had been exploring the reef for an hour when they saw a shark.
The divers had being exploring the reef for an hour when they saw a shark.
questions.why: The past perfect progressive is had been + -ing and fits an action that continued until a past event.

questions.stem: Correct the verb that breaks the past-tense pattern in Yara's story about a kitten.
segments: It is shivering in the cold.
questions.correction: It was shivering in the cold.
questions.why: Keep tenses consistent: the story is in the past, so use the past progressive "was shivering."

questions.stem: Choose the verb that best completes the sentence: By the time Fahad graduates in 2030, he ____ at the same school for twelve years.
options: will be studying
has been studying
had been studying
will have been studying
questions.why: A duration (for twelve years) up to a future point (by 2030) calls for the future perfect progressive.

questions.stem: Select the sentence about Nouf's cooking that uses the present simple.

segments.text: Nouf is mixing the flour now.
Nouf cooks dinner with her mother on Fridays.
Nouf baked bread last week.
Nouf will make kabsa tomorrow.

questions.why: The present simple (cooks) describes a habit or routine.

questions.stem: Which sentences about the Al-Khwarizmi math club use "since" or "for" correctly? Choose two.
options: Members have been solving puzzles since two hours.
The club has met every Tuesday since September.
The club has met every Tuesday for September.
Members have been solving puzzles for two hours.
questions.why: "Since" goes with a starting point (September); "for" goes with a length of time (two hours).

questions.stem: Classify each sentence about the camel race by whether its verb tense is used correctly.

rows.text: The race has started ten minutes ago.
The camels had been running for an hour when the race ended.
By sunset, the winner will have received a trophy.
The riders are training since last winter.

questions.why: Use the past simple with "ago" and the present perfect progressive (have been training) with "since."

questions.stem: True or false: "Sami has already finished his history project" correctly uses "already" with the present perfect.
questions.why: "Already" often goes between has/have and the past participle in the present perfect.

questions.stem: True or false: In "The baby camel was sleeping when the storm began," the verb "was sleeping" is in the past simple.
questions.why: Was + -ing is the past progressive, not the past simple.

questions.stem: Match each verb from Amal's chemistry lab report to its tense.
questions.why: Look at the helping verbs (is, had, will, has been, was) to name each tense.

questions.stem: Correct the tense error in this sentence about the crew of a space mission.
questions.why: "By the time the rocket lands" points to the future, so use the future perfect progressive.

questions.stem: Choose the time expression that best completes the sentence: Waleed hasn't finished his poster about Ibn Sina ____.
options: since
already
ago
yet
questions.why: "Yet" is used with the present perfect in negative sentences and questions.

questions.stem: Which sentences about the trip to the Edge of the World use the future progressive? Choose two.
options: At sunset, Ziad will be taking photos of the valley.
This time tomorrow, we will have driven toward the cliffs.
This time tomorrow, we will be driving toward the cliffs.
At sunset yesterday, Ziad took photos of the valley.
questions.why: Will be + -ing is the future progressive; will have + participle is the future perfect.

questions.stem: Classify each sentence about Al-Jazari and his water clocks by its tense.

rows.text: Al-Jazari designed a famous elephant clock.
Engineers had built water clocks long before Al-Jazari improved them.
Museums have rebuilt models of his machines.
Many students have studied his drawings.

questions.why: Past simple = one past form; past perfect = had + participle; present perfect = has/have + participle.

questions.stem: Which sentence correctly uses the future perfect progressive?
options: By May, Rana will have been training for the marathon for six months.
By May, Rana will been having training for the marathon for six months.
By May, Rana will have be training for the marathon for six months.
By May, Rana will has been training for the marathon for six months.
questions.why: The future perfect progressive is will have been + -ing.

questions.stem: Correct the tense error in this sentence about the desert research team.
questions.why: The past perfect progressive needs a past-time reference point, so the storm "hit."

questions.stem: True or false: In "Since the new library opened, students have borrowed more books," the main clause correctly uses the present perfect with "since."
questions.why: A "since" clause in the past simple pairs with a main clause in the present perfect.

questions.stem: Choose the verb that best completes the sentence: When the coach finally arrived, the players were exhausted because they ____ in the heat for an hour.
options: were waited
will have waited
had been waiting
have been waiting
questions.why: The past perfect progressive explains a past result (exhausted) by an earlier ongoing action.

questions.stem: Which sentences about Ibn Battuta's journeys correctly use the past perfect? Choose two.
options: He had visit Mecca before he reached India.
By the time he returned to Morocco, Ibn Battuta has traveled for decades.
By the time he returned to Morocco, Ibn Battuta had traveled for decades.
He had visited Mecca before he reached India.
questions.why: The past perfect needs had + the past participle (traveled, visited).

questions.stem: Match each sentence about Norah's hospital internship to its tense.

pairs.left: Norah works at the hospital lab on weekends.
Norah is analyzing blood samples this week.
Norah has completed two research reports.
Norah will present her findings in June.

questions.why: Present simple shows routine, present progressive shows a current activity, present perfect shows a completed result, and will shows the future.

questions.stem: Select the two sentences about the class visit to a Riyadh Metro station that shift tense incorrectly. Select two sentences.

segments.text: Last spring, our class toured the new metro station.
The engineer explains how the trains run without drivers.
We watched a train glide into the station.
Afterward, everyone asks questions about the tunnels.

questions.why: A paragraph about a past event should stay in the past tense: explained, asked.

questions.stem: Choose the sentence in which the tenses best show that one past action happened before another.
options: After the team analyzes the data, it had published the results.
After the team has analyzed the data, it published the results.
After the team had analyzed the data, it has published the results.
After the team had analyzed the data, it published the results.
questions.why: The past perfect (had analyzed) marks the earlier action; the past simple (published) marks the later one.

questions.stem: Read: "Dr. Salem will present the vaccine study next month. By then, his team will have been testing the vaccine for a year. Before the testing began, they had spent months designing the trial. They first proposed the idea five years ago." Put the events of Dr. Salem's study in time order, from earliest to latest.
sequence: The team first proposed the idea.
The team spent months designing the trial.
The team began testing the vaccine.
questions.why: Past simple and past perfect describe earlier events; future perfect progressive and future simple describe later ones.

questions.stem: Choose the verb that best completes the sentence: Scientists warn that by 2050 sea levels ____ enough to threaten many coastal towns.
options: had risen
will have risen
have risen
are rising
questions.why: "By 2050" sets a future deadline, so use the future perfect: will have risen.

questions.stem: Classify each sentence from Saud's history report by the tense of its main verb.

rows.text: Historians have been debating the cause for decades.
The city had been growing for centuries before the flood.
By next year, archaeologists will have been digging there for a decade.

questions.why: The helping verbs have been / had been / will have been + -ing name the three perfect progressive tenses.

questions.stem: True or false: In "The committee will be reviewing the applications all next week," the verb is in the future perfect.
questions.why: Will be + -ing is the future progressive; the future perfect is will have + past participle.

questions.stem: Correct the tense error in this sentence about the solar farm in Sakaka.
questions.why: A main clause with "since" needs the present perfect: has provided.

questions.stem: Read the sentence: "By the time the delegation arrives in Tokyo, the engineers will have been refining the design for eighteen months." Which tense is "will have been refining"?

partA.stem: Read the sentence: "By the time the delegation arrives in Tokyo, the engineers will have been refining the design for eighteen months." Which tense is "will have been refining"?

partB.stem: Which statement best supports the answer about the engineers' sentence?

options.label: A
options.text: The action began in the past and is continuing at present.

options.label: B
options.text: The action continues for a period up to a point in the future.

options.label: C
options.text: The action will be in progress at one single moment in the future.

options.label: D
options.text: The action will be complete before a future time, with no duration.

questions.why: The future perfect progressive stresses duration (for eighteen months) up to a future point (by the time the delegation arrives).

questions.stem: Which sentences from Reema's report on water desalination use tense correctly? Choose two.
options: Before the first large plant opened, coastal towns had relied on wells.
Saudi Arabia has been building desalination plants for decades.
By the time the first plant opened, engineers have studied the problem for years.
Today, the plants had been producing much of the country's water.
questions.why: Match the tense to the time: has been building connects past to now, and had relied marks an earlier past.

questions.stem: Which revision correctly fixes the tense error in this sentence: "Hind has written her thesis on Al-Razi when her advisor retired last year."
options: Hind will have written her thesis on Al-Razi when her advisor retired last year.
Hind was writing her thesis on Al-Razi when her advisor retired last year.
Hind writes her thesis on Al-Razi when her advisor retired last year.
Hind has been writing her thesis on Al-Razi when her advisor retired last year.
questions.why: An action in progress when another past action happened takes the past progressive (was writing).

questions.stem: Match each sentence about Mansour's chess career to the tense of its main verb.

pairs.left: Mansour had been playing for five years before he won a title.
Mansour will be competing in Baku next week.
Mansour won his first national title in 2022.
Mansour has been coaching young players lately.
By 2030, Mansour will have played in fifty tournaments.

questions.why: Each tense has its own helping-verb pattern: had been + -ing, will be + -ing, past form, has been + -ing, will have + participle.

questions.stem: Choose the verb that best completes the sentence: If the rains continue, by next spring the wadi ____ water for three straight months.
options: has been carrying
would be carrying
will have been carrying
had been carrying
questions.why: A duration measured up to a future point (by next spring) takes the future perfect progressive.

questions.stem: Is each sentence about the school garden in the active voice or the passive voice?

rows.text: Huda waters the mint plants every morning.
The mint plants are watered every morning.
The tomatoes were picked by the fourth graders.
The fourth graders picked the tomatoes.

questions.why: In the passive voice, the subject receives the action and the verb uses a form of be + past participle.

questions.stem: Choose the verb that makes the sentence passive: The classroom windows ____ every Thursday.
options: cleaning
clean
is cleaned
are cleaned
questions.why: A plural subject in the present simple passive needs are + past participle.

questions.stem: Which sentence correctly changes "Omar painted the fence." to the passive voice?
options: The fence is painted by Omar.
The fence was painted by Omar.
The fence painted by Omar.
Omar was painted by the fence.
questions.why: Past simple active becomes was/were + past participle, and the object becomes the subject.

questions.stem: True or false: The sentence "The camel race will be held on Friday." is in the passive voice.
questions.why: Will be + past participle (will be held) is the future simple passive.

questions.stem: Find and fix the error in the passive sentence about the science fair prizes.
questions.why: The future passive needs will be + the past participle, so give must become given.

questions.stem: Which two sentences about the date harvest are in the passive voice? Choose two.
options: The farmers packed the dates into boxes.
The workers were tired after the harvest.
The dates were packed into boxes.
The palm trees are watered by a drip system.
questions.why: Were tired is be + an adjective, not be + a past participle that shows an action done to the subject.

questions.stem: Complete the sentence with the past simple passive: The old bridge ____ in 1990.
options: is built
was build
built
was built
questions.why: The past simple passive is was/were + past participle (built).

questions.stem: Match each active sentence about the librarian with its passive form.

pairs.right: The books are stamped by the librarian.
The books were stamped by the librarian.

pairs.left: The librarian will stamp the books.
pairs.right: The books will be stamped by the librarian.

questions.why: The passive keeps the tense of the active verb: stamps → are stamped, stamped → were stamped, will stamp → will be stamped.

questions.stem: Which sentence correctly changes "The chef will bake the bread in the morning." to the passive voice?
options: The chef will be baked by the bread in the morning.
The bread will been baked by the chef in the morning.
The bread will be baked by the chef in the morning.
The bread will bake by the chef in the morning.
questions.why: Future simple active (will bake) becomes will be + past participle (will be baked).

questions.stem: Put the parts in order to form a present progressive passive sentence about the new hospital.
questions.why: The present progressive passive uses is/are being + past participle, followed by the by-phrase.

questions.stem: Classify each sentence about the museum trip as active or passive.

rows.text: The guide was showing us old coins.
The old coins were being cleaned when we arrived.
The students are being guided through the hall.
The students are walking through the hall.

questions.why: Being + past participle (being cleaned, being guided) signals a progressive passive.

questions.stem: Choose the present progressive passive form: Right now, the football field ____ for tonight's match.
options: is being painted
is painting
is been painted
was painted
questions.why: An action happening now to the subject uses is being + past participle.

questions.stem: Which sentence about the solar panels is written in the present perfect passive?
options: The solar panels have been installed on the roof.
The workers have installed the solar panels on the roof.
The solar panels are being installed on the roof.
The solar panels were installed on the roof.
questions.why: The present perfect passive is has/have been + past participle.

questions.stem: Find and fix the error in the passive sentence about the bus to the zoo.
questions.why: The passive needs the past participle driven, not the past tense drove.

questions.stem: True or false: In the sentence "The letters are sorted by machines every night," the doer of the action is "machines."
questions.why: In a passive sentence, the doer (agent) appears after by.

questions.stem: Match each tense name with the correct passive form of the verb "build."
questions.why: Every passive form ends with the past participle built; only the form of be changes with the tense.

questions.stem: Which two sentences correctly use the past progressive passive? Choose two.
options: The old map was being repaired in the lab.
The camels were feeding when the storm began.
The camels were being fed when the storm began.
The old map was been repaired in the lab.
questions.why: The past progressive passive is was/were being + past participle.

questions.stem: Choose the correct passive form: When the guests arrived, the dinner ____ already.
options: had been served
had served
has been served
was serving
questions.why: An action finished before another past action uses the past perfect passive: had been + past participle.

questions.stem: Which sentence about the Red Sea coral reef is written in the passive voice?
options: Divers are visiting the coral reef today.
The coral reef is home to many fish.
Strict laws protect the coral reef.
The coral reef is protected by strict laws.
questions.why: Is protected is be + past participle, so the reef receives the action.

questions.stem: For each passive sentence about the lost bicycle, tell whether the agent is named.

rows.text: My bicycle was lost near the park.
The bicycle was found by a police officer.
The bicycle was returned to me on Sunday.
The report was written by Officer Fahad.

questions.why: The agent is named only when a by-phrase tells who did the action.

questions.stem: Find and fix the error in the present perfect passive sentence about the new road.
questions.why: The present perfect passive uses has been, not has being.

questions.stem: Put the parts of this future perfect passive sentence about the metro line in order.
questions.why: The future perfect passive is will have been + past participle.

questions.stem: Choose the modal passive that completes the safety rule: Lab goggles ____ during every experiment.
options: must worn
must wear
must be worn
must be wear
questions.why: A modal passive is modal + be + past participle (must be worn).

questions.stem: Which sentence correctly changes "Engineers had tested the new engine before the flight." to the passive voice?
options: The new engine had been tested by engineers before the flight.
The new engine was being tested by engineers before the flight.
Engineers had been tested by the new engine before the flight.
The new engine has been tested by engineers before the flight.
questions.why: Past perfect active (had tested) becomes had been + past participle.

questions.stem: True or false: "The exam results will have been posted by noon" is an example of the future perfect passive.
questions.why: Will have been + past participle is the future perfect passive.

questions.stem: Which three sentences about the science lab are in the passive voice? Choose three.
options: The teacher was recording the data every hour.
The samples have been labeled carefully.
The class should rinse the beakers after use.
The beakers should be rinsed after use.
The data was being recorded every hour.
The students have labeled the samples carefully.
questions.why: Each passive sentence uses a form of be + past participle, and the subject receives the action.

questions.stem: Classify each sentence about the date festival by its voice.

rows.text: The festival is organized every winter.
Families visit the festival every winter.
Prizes were given to the best farmers.
The judges gave prizes to the best farmers.

questions.why: Is organized and were given are be + past participle, so those sentences are passive.

questions.stem: Find and fix the error in the modal passive sentence about borrowing library books.
questions.why: A modal passive needs be between the modal and the past participle.

questions.stem: Match each sentence about the airport runway with the name of its passive tense.

pairs.left: The runway will have been extended.

questions.why: The helping verbs before extended (is being, was being, has been, will have been) show the tense.

questions.stem: Choose the past progressive passive form: While the school hall ____, the students waited outside.
options: is being cleaned
was cleaning
was being cleaned
has been cleaned
questions.why: An action in progress in the past that is done to the subject uses was being + past participle.

questions.stem: Why is the passive voice a good choice in the lab sentence "The water was heated to 100 degrees Celsius"?
options: The active voice cannot be used in a sentence with numbers.
The passive voice makes the action seem to happen faster.
The writer wants to show exactly who heated the water.
The person who heated the water is not important.
questions.why: Science reports often use the passive because the action and result matter more than the doer.

questions.stem: For each sentence about the AlUla excavation, choose the tense of the passive verb.

rows.text: Ancient tools have been found at the site.
The site had been buried for centuries before its discovery.
The findings will have been studied by next summer.
Several tombs have been mapped this year.

questions.why: Have been, had been, and will have been mark the present, past, and future perfect passive.

questions.stem: Find and fix the error in the past perfect passive sentence about the football tournament.
questions.why: The past perfect passive needs the past participle cleaned after had been.

questions.stem: Which two sentences use the passive voice because the doer of the action is unknown? Choose two.
options: The coins were hidden by the merchant's son.
The museum displays the coins in a glass case.
The ancient coins were hidden under the floor centuries ago.
The shop window was broken during the night.
questions.why: The passive without a by-phrase is useful when no one knows who did the action.

questions.stem: Complete the present simple passive sentence: Arabic coffee ____ to guests in small cups.
options: serves
is serving
is served
are served
questions.why: A singular subject in the present simple passive takes is + past participle.

questions.stem: Which sentence correctly changes "The committee is reviewing the new proposal." to the passive voice?
options: The new proposal is reviewed by the committee.
The new proposal is being reviewed by the committee.
The committee is being reviewed by the new proposal.
The new proposal has being reviewed by the committee.
questions.why: Present progressive active (is reviewing) becomes is being + past participle.

questions.stem: True or false: The sentence "The bridge must be inspected every year" is in the active voice because it contains the modal "must."
questions.why: Must be inspected is modal + be + past participle, which is a modal passive.

questions.stem: Select the sentence about the desalination plant that uses the future perfect passive.

segments.text: The plant will produce fresh water for the city.
By 2030, enough fresh water will have been produced for the whole city.
Engineers have built three new pipelines.
More pipelines will be added next year.

questions.why: Will have been produced is will have been + past participle, the future perfect passive.

questions.stem: Find and fix the error in the present progressive passive sentence about the stadium lights.
questions.why: The present progressive passive needs being: are being + past participle.

questions.stem: Match each active sentence about the satellite with its passive version.

pairs.right: The satellite was launched by scientists.
The satellite has been launched by scientists.
The satellite had been launched by scientists.

pairs.left: Scientists will have launched the satellite.
pairs.right: The satellite will have been launched by scientists.

questions.why: The passive keeps the active tense and adds a form of be before the past participle launched.

questions.stem: Which two sentences correctly use a modal passive? Choose two.
options: The samples might been damaged during transport.
The samples might have been damaged during transport.
The forms should be submitted before Thursday.
The forms should be submit before Thursday.
questions.why: A modal passive is modal + be + past participle, or modal + have been + past participle for the past.

questions.stem: Choose the verb that keeps the lab report in the passive voice: The solution ____ for ten minutes, and then its temperature was recorded.
options: is stirred
was stirred
was stirring
stirred
questions.why: The report is in the past, and the solution receives the action, so was + past participle is needed.

questions.stem: Decide whether each lab-report sentence about the seedling experiment is active or passive.

rows.text: The seedlings were placed near a window.
We measured the seedlings every day.
The height of each plant was recorded.
The tallest seedling grew 12 centimeters.

questions.why: Were placed and was recorded are be + past participle; measured and grew are active verbs.

questions.stem: A lab report states, "We poured the salt water into the beaker." Which revision uses the passive voice expected in a formal report?
options: We had poured the salt water into the beaker.
The beaker was poured into the salt water.
The salt water poured into the beaker.
The salt water was poured into the beaker.
questions.why: Formal reports often focus on the material, so the object becomes the subject with was + past participle.

questions.stem: Find and fix the error in the future perfect passive sentence about the marathon.
segments: By the time the runners finish,
questions.why: The future perfect passive is will have been + past participle.

questions.stem: Which sentence correctly changes "By sunset, the crew will have unloaded all the cargo." to the passive voice?
options: By sunset, all the cargo will be unloaded by the crew.
By sunset, all the cargo will have been unloaded by the crew.
By sunset, all the cargo will have unloaded by the crew.
By sunset, the crew will have been unloaded by all the cargo.
questions.why: Future perfect active (will have unloaded) becomes will have been + past participle.

questions.stem: Part A: What are the voice and tense of the verb in "The vaccine had been tested on thousands of volunteers before approval"?

partA.stem: Part A: What are the voice and tense of the verb in "The vaccine had been tested on thousands of volunteers before approval"?

partB.stem: Part B: Which sentence expresses the same idea in the active voice?

options.label: A
options.text: Researchers tested the vaccine on thousands of volunteers after approval.

options.label: B
options.text: Researchers have tested the vaccine on thousands of volunteers before approval.

options.label: C
options.text: Researchers had tested the vaccine on thousands of volunteers before approval.

options.label: D
options.text: The vaccine had tested thousands of volunteers before approval.

questions.why: Had been tested is the past perfect passive; its active form is had tested with the doer as subject.

questions.stem: True or false: "The ancient manuscript is being restored by experts in Riyadh" uses the past progressive passive.
questions.why: Is being restored is the present progressive passive; the past form would be was being restored.

questions.stem: Classify each sentence about the Hejaz Railway by the tense of its passive verb.

rows.text: The railway was opened in 1908.
Supplies were being carried north along the line.
Many stations had been finished before the first train arrived.
Some old carriages were restored in recent years.

questions.why: Was/were + participle is past simple, was/were being + participle is past progressive, and had been + participle is past perfect.

questions.stem: Choose the verb that correctly completes the sentence: By the time the director arrives, all the contracts ____.
options: had been signed
will have signed
will have been signed
will be signing
questions.why: An action completed before a future moment, done to the subject, uses the future perfect passive.
